verdict.reasoning: Both quotations are accurate, but the difference is page-break furniture placement, which the rubric excludes. VERIFIED FACTS: (1) The rendered PDF page 1018 (printed 988) does open with 'Old_Italic:' on its own line followed by '10300-1031F, 1032D-1032F'. (2) The rendered PDF page 1017 (printed 987) ends with 'Old_Hungarian:' / '10C80-10CB2, 10CC0-10CF2' and does NOT contain 'Old_Italic:'. (3) specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 40558 is exactly '10C80-10CB2, 10CC0-10CF2 Old_Italic:'. So the label did move to the far side of the page marker. REFUTATION: (a) NO TEXT IS LOST OR ALTERED. Every token on PDF page 1018 is present in the markdown, and a full entry-by-entry diff of all 16 script entries on the page (Old_Italic, Old_North_Arabian, Old_Permic, Old_Persian, Old_Sogdian, Old_South_Arabian, Old_Turkic, Oriya, Osage, Osmanya, Pahawh_Hmong, Palmyrene, Pau_Cin_Hau, Phags_Pa, Phoenician, Psalter_Pahlavi) matches the PDF character for character. (b) READING ORDER IS PRESERVED, so the binding is NOT destroyed. The markdown token sequence is 'Old_Hungarian:' / '10C80-10CB2, 10CC0-10CF2' / 'Old_Italic:' / [page anchor + running head] / '10300-1031F, 1032D-1032F' -- identical to the PDF's sequence except for where the page marker falls. 'Old_Italic:' still immediately precedes its own ranges and follows Old_Hungarian's; it did not jump over any other script entry. The only real change is one line break and the side of the page anchor the label sits on. (c) The claim's own premise concedes the union of code points is unchanged, and its harm argument rests entirely on a hypothetical naive line-based extractor rather than on the content differing. (d) DECISIVE: this is uniform transcription-pipeline behavior, not a page-1018 content error. Scanning the page anchors across Annex B shows the first script label of page N+1 appended to the last range line of page N at essentially every boundary: page-1011 '1E900-1E943, 1E94B Ahom:', page-1012 '1A00-1A16 Buhid:', page-1015 'A984-A9B2 Kaithi:', page-1016 '...10760-10767 Linear_B:', page-1017 '10980-1099F Miao:', page-1018 '...10CC0-10CF2 Old_Italic:', page-1019 '10B80-10B91 Rejang:', page-1020 'Tai_Le:', page-1021 'Yezidi:', page-1022 '1A17-1A1B Buhid:', page-1023 '0AFA-0AFF Gunjala_Gondi:', page-1024 '...17E0-17E9 Khojki:', page-1025 '...11650-11659 Mongolian:'. Confirmed against the PDF at both adjacent boundaries: page 1018's PDF ends at 'Psalter_Pahlavi:' / '10B80-10B91' with no 'Rejang:', and page 1019's markdown correspondingly opens with the headless 'A930-A946'. Filing this as a per-page content discrepancy would mint an identical ledger entry at every page boundary in the annex. It belongs in the reconciliation record, if anywhere, as a single pipeline-level formatting note about page-boundary line joining -- not as a page-1018 content defect. REMAINING CAVEAT (formatting, not content): the glued line '10C80-10CB2, 10CC0-10CF2 Old_Italic:' would mis-bind under a strictly line-oriented extractor that ignores the page anchors. Any tool consuming Annex B must split on the page-anchor furniture, which it must do anyway for the running heads and the '988 (c)ISO/IEC 2023' footers. That is a consumer-robustness requirement, not a discrepancy between the PDF and the markdown.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a content discrepancy. The claim's two quotations are accurate, but nothing is missing, added, or reordered: 'Old_Italic:' is present on the adjacent line, still immediately preceding its own range '10300-1031F, 1032D-1032F' in reading order and still following Old_Hungarian's range. The sole difference is which side of the page-break furniture the label falls on, i.e. line wrapping at the page join. It is also not specific to page 1018: the transcription appends the next page's first script label to the previous page's last range line at every Annex B page boundary (verified at 1011, 1012, 1015-1025). If tracked at all, track it once as a pipeline-level page-boundary line-joining note, with the guidance that Annex B extraction must split on the page anchors.
